title: How do we find every angle between the rays on a protractor?
description: Six rays leave the centre of a protractor, and the scale that starts at zero on the first ray gives a reading for each of the others. Angles with the first ray are read directly, and every other angle is found by subtracting two readings. Keeko's doubt, that the two readings should be added, is broken by showing a part that would be bigger than its whole.
teaching_notes: One idea: with a common zero ray, the angle between two other rays is the larger reading minus the smaller reading. Watch for children who add the readings.

source: Name the different angles in the figure and write their meas
video_script.why: The child finds the measure of every angle between six rays on a protractor, using readings from one zero ray and subtraction.
video_script.substitution: The book's labelled protractor with the rays OP, OQ, OR, OS, OT and OU.
video_script.anchor: the book's labelled protractor with six rays OP, OQ, OR, OS, OT and OU leaving the centre O
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says to add the two readings to get the angle between two rays. The two rays lie inside a bigger angle, and a part cannot be bigger than the whole, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: P O Q is thirty five, and P O R is ninety five degrees. P O S is one hundred and twenty five degrees. P O T is one hundred and sixty degrees. Q O R is sixty, and Q O S is ninety degrees. Q O T is one hundred and twenty five degrees. Q O U is one hundred and forty five degrees. R O S is thirty, and R O T is sixty five degrees. R O U is eighty five degrees. S O T is thirty five, and S O U is fifty five degrees. T O U is twenty degrees.

final_answer.spoken: the angles with O P are thirty five, ninety five, one hundred and twenty five and one hundred and sixty degrees, and the other angles are found by subtracting two readings

maths_rules: reading from P as zero: Q = 35, R = 95, S = 125, T = 160, U = 180
angles with OP are the readings: POQ = 35, POR = 95, POS = 125, POT = 160
other angles are the larger reading minus the smaller reading
P, O and U lie in one line, so POU is a straight angle, and it is not one of the listed angles
video_script.design: One protractor with six rays stays on the board. The readings are written once from P as zero, and each angle is then shaded and labelled as it is found.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: read each ray on the scale that starts at 0 on OP: Q at 35°, R at 95°, S at 125°, T at 160°, U at 180° (P, O, U lie in one line)

<bookmark mark='qr'/>Q is at thirty five and R is at ninety five. S is at one hundred and twenty five.
<bookmark mark='tu'/>T is at one hundred and sixty. U is at one hundred and eighty, so P, O and U lie in one line.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: a reading is the angle from OP: ∠POQ = 35°, ∠POR = 95°, ∠POS = 125°, ∠POT = 160°

<bookmark mark='pq'/>P O Q is thirty five degrees, and P O R is ninety five. P O S and P O T are read the same way.

marks.rest: the other nine subtractions are written below one after another

beats.moves_through: the angle between each pair of rays is shaded as its subtraction appears
narration: <bookmark mark='sub'/>Step three, take two other rays and subtract the smaller reading from the larger. For Q O R, ninety five minus thirty five is sixty.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Do this for every other pair of rays.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check: ∠QOR and ∠ROS side by side fill ∠QOS; 60° + 30° = 90°

narration: <bookmark mark='fill'/>Step four, check with a part and a whole. Q O R and R O S sit side by side and together fill Q O S.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Sixty plus thirty is ninety, which matches Q O S.
<bookmark mark='a'/>P O Q is thirty five, and P O R is ninety five degrees.
<bookmark mark='b'/>P O S is one hundred and twenty five degrees. P O T is one hundred and sixty degrees.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Q O R is sixty, and Q O S is ninety degrees.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Q O T is one hundred and twenty five degrees. Q O U is one hundred and forty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='e'/>R O S is thirty, and R O T is sixty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='f'/>R O U is eighty five degrees. S O T is thirty five, and S O U is fifty five degrees. T O U is twenty degrees.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the protractor
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt: add the two readings; for QOR, 35° + 95° = 130°, but QOR sits inside POR = 95°; a part cannot be bigger than the whole; the doubt is crossed out

marks.sum: 35° + 95° = 130° is written for Q O R
marks.whole: Q O R is shown inside P O R and the doubt is crossed out

beats.moves_through: the shaded angle Q O R slides inside the angle P O R
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko says to add the two readings to get the angle between two rays.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>For Q O R, that gives thirty five plus ninety five, or one hundred and thirty.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>But Q O R sits inside P O R, which is only ninety five. A part cannot be bigger than the whole.
